questions.q: According to the biblical account of creation in Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
options: The sun, moon, and stars
Light
Land animals
The firmament
questions.explain: In **Genesis 1:3**, God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light. This occurred on the **first day** of creation.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did God bring the universe into existence according to the Genesis account?
options: By physically molding the earth with His hands
Through the spoken word
By combining water and fire
Through a slow process of evolution
questions.explain: Throughout Genesis 1, God created the universe primarily through the **spoken word** (e.g., 'And God said...').
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: On which day did God create human beings, according to Genesis chapter 1?
options: Third day
Fourth day
Fifth day
Sixth day
questions.explain: According to **Genesis 1:26-31**, God created land animals and human beings (male and female) on the **sixth day**.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What was the initial state of the earth before God began the work of creation? (Genesis 1:2)
options: It was filled with prehistoric animals.
It was formless and void, and darkness covered the deep.
It was a beautiful garden with no inhabitants.
It was entirely covered with dry land.
questions.explain: **Genesis 1:2** states: 'The earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Genesis 2, how did God give life to the first man after forming him from the dust of the ground?
options: He gave him fruit from the Tree of Life to eat.
He commanded angels to wake him up.
He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.
He washed him in the river of Eden.
questions.explain: **Genesis 2:7** explains that after forming man from the dust, God 'breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.'

questions.q: God created the sun, moon, and stars on the fourth day. What was their primary purpose according to Genesis?
options: To give light to the earth and separate day from night
To serve as homes for the angels
To provide warmth for the animals
To dry up the waters and create land
questions.explain: In **Genesis 1:14-15**, God created the celestial lights 'to separate the day from the night' and 'to give light upon the earth'.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What did God do on the seventh day of the creation week?
options: He created Eve.
He planted the Garden of Eden.
He rested from all His work.
He made a covenant with Adam.
questions.explain: According to **Genesis 2:2-3**, God finished His work and **rested on the seventh day**, blessing it and making it holy.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)

questions.q: What is the primary theme of songs about creation sung in English and different Nigerian languages?
options: To mourn the fall of man
To praise and acknowledge God's awesome power as the Creator
To teach people how to farm
To remember the history of early missionaries
questions.explain: Creation songs are hymns of **adoration and praise** that celebrate the beauty of nature and acknowledge God's absolute sovereignty and creative power.

questions.q: After creating all things, God looked at everything He had made. How did He describe it in Genesis 1:31?
options: He said it was acceptable.
He saw that it was very good.
He felt it needed improvement.
He declared it completely perfect and unchangeable.
questions.explain: In **Genesis 1:31**, 'God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was **very good**.'

questions.q: According to Genesis 2, why did God create the woman (Eve)?
options: To compete with the man for leadership.
To be a suitable helper and companion for the man.
To rule over the animals in the sea.
To discover fire for the man.
questions.explain: In **Genesis 2:18**, God said, 'It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a **helper fit for him**.'
